DECISION
Introduction

Summary

Pursuant to the General Statutes of Connecticut §16-32e, the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority reviewed the public service companies’ plans for restoration of interrupted service resulting from an emergency. The Public Utilities Regulatory Authority finds that most companies filed their emergency plans in compliance with the Statute. In this Decision, the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority directs non-compliant subject companies to file their Emergency Plans or to revise, as appropriate, and resubmit their plans to meet the new requirements and include recommendations made by the Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection and the Department of Public Health to enhance their Emergency Plans.

Background of the Proceeding

Section 16-32e(b) of the General Statutes of Connecticut (Conn. Gen. Stat. or Statute) requires each public service company, telecommunications company, voice over Internet protocol (VoIP) service provider, and municipal utility furnishing electric, gas or water service to file every two years an updated plan for restoring utility service that is interrupted as a result of an emergency (Emergency Plan). The Statute also requires that the Emergency Plans be filed with the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (Authority or PURA), the Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection (DESPP) and each municipality located within the service area of the public service company, telecommunications company, VoIP service provider or municipal utility. In addition, each water company is further required to file Emergency Plans with the Department of Public Health (DPH), the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP), the Office of Policy and Management and each regional planning organization covering any portion of the company's existing or proposed source or service area.

On April 1, 2014, the Authority initiated this docket, as an uncontested case to oversee the submission and review of the Emergency Plans. The Statute requires that the Emergency Plans to be filed by July 1, 2014. It also requires that the Authority, on or before September 1, 2012, and biannually thereafter, submit a report, in accordance with Conn. Gen. Stat. §11-4a to the joint standing committee of the General Assembly having cognizance of matters relating to public utilities summarizing such plans.

Conduct of the Proceeding
By Notice of Proceeding and Request for Emergency Plans dated June 4, 2014, the Authority requested each public service company, telecommunications company, each VoIP service provider and each municipal utility to file, by July 1, 2014, with the Authority, the DESPP and each municipality located within the service area of the public service company et al, an updated plan for restoring service that is interrupted as a result of an emergency.

Public service companies or municipal utilities that submit a water supply plan pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §25-32d are not required to submit emergency service restoration plans in this proceeding. However, the Authority directed that such providers submit to the PURA an acknowledgment of its exemption in writing.

The Authority also indicated that telecommunications providers that do not install, maintain, operate or control poles, wires, conduits or other fixtures under and over a public highway for the provision of telecommunications service authorized by Conn. Gen. Stat. §16-247c are not required to file an emergency service restoration plan. The Authority directed that such providers submit to the PURA an acknowledgment of its exemption in writing.

As of July 24, 2014, not all Emergency Plans were filed by the companies. By Second Notice of Proceeding and Request for Emergency Plans dated July 25, 2014, the Authority directed all participants to file emergency service restoration plans or revised plans with the Authority that satisfy all of the requirements of Conn. Gen. Stat. §16-32e on or before July 31, 2014.

A Draft Decision was issued on August 22, 2014. All participants were given the opportunity to submit written exceptions.

Participants

The Authority designated the Office of Consumer Counsel, the Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection, the Department of Public Health, the Connecticut General Assembly Energy and Technology Committee, all public service companies, telecommunications companies, VoIP service providers, and municipal utilities furnishing electric, gas or water service as participants to this proceeding. A listing of all participants is appended hereto as Appendix A.
Emergency Plan Review

Statutory Requirements For Emergency Plans

Conn. Gen. Stat. §16-32e(b), requires each Emergency Plan to include measures for (1) communication and coordination with state officials, municipalities and other public service companies and telecommunications companies during a major disaster, as defined in Conn. Gen. Stat. §28-1, or an emergency; and (2) participation in training exercises as directed by the Commissioner of DESPP. Each such plan must include the company, provider or municipal utility response proposal for service outages affecting more than 10%, 30%, 50%, and 70% of their customers. The Authority received and reviewed the public service companies’ Emergency Plans filed pursuant to the Statute. A listing of the companies filing reports or exemptions is provided in Appendix B. In event that the Authority revises any emergency plan filed pursuant to the Statute, then the affected company/municipal utility must file a copy of their revised plan with each municipality located within their respective service area.
The Statute also requires that, at the discretion of the Commissioner of DESPP or after an emergency or major disaster is declared in the state by the Governor under the laws of this state or by the President of the United States under federal law, each telephone company, certified telecommunications provider, holders of a certificate of video franchise authority (CVFA) and holders of certificates of cable franchise authority (CCFA), with more than 25,000 subscribers, shall provide a representative to staff the emergency operations center of an affected electric distribution company, as needed to ensure communication and coordination during emergency response and restoration efforts.

Cable Certificate Holders

The Authority received and reviewed the Emergency Plans submitted by holders of a CVFA and CCFA serving Connecticut. With the exception of revisions and requirements indicated below, the Authority finds the Emergency Plans filed by the holders of a CCVA and CCFA have met the statutory requirements.

Electric

The Authority received and reviewed the Emergency Plans filed by two privately owned electric companies and two of the six Connecticut municipal electric utilities. The Authority finds that The Connecticut Light and Power Company (CL&P), The United Illuminating Company (UI), Jewett City Department of Public Utilities and Norwich Public Utilities Emergency Plans have met the requirements and the 2012 recommendations described below.

The City of Groton Department of Public Utility, the Norwalk 3rd Taxing District, South Norwalk Electric and Water and the Town of Wallingford Department of Public Utility did not provide Emergency Plans. The Authority will direct these municipal electric utilities to submit a compliant Emergency Plan by September 19, 2014.

Natural Gas

The Authority received and reviewed the Emergency Plans submitted by the state’s natural gas companies. The Southern Connecticut Natural Gas Company (SCG) and Connecticut Natural Gas Corporation (CNG) submitted their Gas Emergency Plans on June 27, 2014. Yankee Gas Services Company (Yankee) submitted its Gas Emergency Plan on June 24, 2014, and Norwich Public Utilities (Norwich) submitted its Gas Emergency Plan on July 9, 2014. The Authority finds that the SCG, CNG and Yankee Emergency Plans have met the requirements and the 2012 recommendations described below. However, the Authority finds that Norwich should expand its Emergency Plan to clarify restoration requirements.

The Authority finds that Norwich’s Emergency Plan did not address large outages. The Norwich’s Emergency Plan needs to include the number of personnel that are necessary for the restoration of natural gas outages and the associated restoration time for each emergency event level required by the Statute. The Authority will order Norwich to update the missing parameters in its Emergency Plan.

Telecommunications Companies and VoIP Providers

The Authority received and reviewed the Emergency Plans submitted by the incumbent local exchange carriers (ILECs), competitive local exchange carriers (CLECs) and VoIP service providers. The Authority notes that the ILECs and some CLECs are providing VoIP services through various IP platforms. With the exception of revisions and additions required below, the Authority finds the above companies’ Emergency Plans have generally met the statutory requirements provided for in the Statute.
Water

Public service companies or municipal utilities that submit a water supply plan (WSP) pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §25-32d were not required to file an Emergency Plan. Since WSPs are only submitted and approved by the DPH every three years, the Authority requested that each water company submit an exemption acknowledgment for not filing an Emergency Plan. The Authority encourages all service companies and municipal utilities to continuously monitor conditions to update their emergency contingencies plans to ensure that the most updated information is included in their respective Emergency Plans.
All water companies, except for the exempted companies, were directed to file Emergency Plans or revised plans with the Authority to satisfy the requirements of the Statute. The Authority did not receive any Emergency Plans from any public service company or municipal water utility in this proceeding. However, the Authority found that most of the private owned water companies and municipal water utilities include their Emergency Plans in their water supply plans. A summary of companies having WSPs and the filing of exemption forms are listed below and show that 51 of 56 privately owned water companies and municipal water utilities have Emergency Plans through their WSPs.

Authority’s Emergency Plan Requirements

The next biennial filing of Emergency Plans is due no later than July 1, 2016. In the Decision dated November 1, 2012, Docket No. 12-06-09, PURA Establishment of Industry Performance Standards for Electric and Gas Companies (Docket No. 12-06-09 Decision), the Authority established standards for acceptable performance in an emergency in which more than 10% of any utility's customers are without service for more than 48 consecutive hours. CL&P, UI, YGS, CNG and SCG were ordered to incorporate into their Emergency Plans, the Performance Standards established in the Docket No. 12-06-09 Decision Appendices A and B, as appropriate, and to implement them in their manner of operations.

By letter dated December 30, 2013, UI reported that it is fully compliant with the EDC Emergency Performance Standards. CL&P reported by letter dated June 24, 2014, that it was in compliance with all requirements of the performance standards.

CNG and SCG reported that they are fully compliant with the Natural Gas Local Distribution Company Emergency Performance Standards with the exception of Section 3.6 Restoration Targets which is expected to be completed by December 31, 2015. CNG and SCG Compliance Letter, December 26, 2013.

YGS reported that it will be in compliance with the Natural Gas Local Distribution Company Emergency Performance Standards by September 30, 2014. YGS Compliance Letter, June 19, 2014.

Similarly, by the Decision dated August 14, 2013 in Docket No. 12-06-10, PURA Establishment of Industry Performance Standards for Telecommunications Companies (Docket No. 12-06-10 Decision), the PURA established standards for telecommunications company service restoration after any emergency. All facilitiesbased intrastate telecommunications service providers were directed to incorporate the standards set forth in the Docket No. 12-06-10 Decision in their respective Emergency Plans. The Authority notes that the following companies included in their Emergency Plans with a Connecticut-specific supplemental plan: The Southern New England Telephone Company d/b/a AT&T Connecticut; Teleport Communications America, LLC; Verizon New York, Inc.; MCI Communications Services, Inc.; MCImetro Access Transmission Services, LLC; Metrocast Communications of CT; Comcast of Connecticut; Fiber Technologies Networks; Cablevision Lightpath - CT, LLC, Level 3 Communications, and Zayo Group International.

Recommendations from State agencies
Pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §1632e(b), the Authority may conduct public hearings on Emergency Plans and, in consultation with the DESPP, the DPH and the joint standing committee of the General Assembly having cognizance of matters relating to public utilities, and revise such plans to the extent necessary to provide properly for the public convenience, necessity and welfare. If the Authority revises the emergency plan of a public service company, telecommunications company, VoIP provider or municipal utility, such company, provider or municipal utility shall file a copy of the revised plan with each municipality located within the service area of the company, provider or municipal utility. By Letter dated August 6, 2014, the Authority requested comments from the Energy and Technology Committee, DESPP and DPH regarding the Emergency Plans filed by the companies in this proceeding. As of this date, no comments were received from state officials.

By the Decision dated August 31, 2012 in Docket No. 12-06-11 PURA Review of Connecticut Public Service Companies Plans for restoration of Service that is Interrupted as a Result of an Emergency (2012 Decision), the Authority suggested companies incorporate the DESPP and the DPH’s recommendations concerning the utility company emergency plans. The DESPP recommended that the Emergency Plans should:

Refer to and incorporate by reference the All Hazards Energy and Utilities Annex to the State Response Framework (Annex). The Annex provides details on the flow of communications and will help to link the various plans together. The Annex describes in detail, the Multi-Agency Coordination that will take place under the Connecticut State Response Framework, specific to utility-related aspects of disasters and emergencies, in order to facilitate restoration and maintenance of the state’s energy, utility, electric, gas, water, waste water, and telecommunications public services during and following a major disaster, such as a hurricane, winter storm, flooding, earthquake or other significant event requiring state assistance.

Indicate an agreement to provide municipal officials at their local Emergency Operations Centers (EOC), as well as the Governor’s state EOC with real-time situational reporting and data from the public service companies invoked in the restoration process. It is imperative that the municipalities and the State receive accurate and timely information on restoration work and status.

2012 Decision, p. 7.

In addition, the DPH recommended that water companies should focus on preparation and service to the state’s critical need priority customers (CNPC) and general comments for all Emergency Plans. Each public service water company should complete the following items for public health CNPCs within its specific Emergency Plan. Those were:

Customers should be prioritized for service and return of service based upon public health need.

Priority for service that concern the DPH are CNPCs such as hospitals, nursing homes, other critical care facilities, public water system and waste water infrastructure (i.e., treatment plants and pump stations), individual customers with critical care needs including those customers with medical device needs such as oxygen and electric powered medical equipment, etc.

Emergency Plans should adequately:

Identify CNPCs including direct points of contact for each CNPC;
Provide for consistent and continued communications with CNPCs during normal and emergency situations;
Plan for direct communication to CNPCs concerning return of service;
Be exercised working with CNPCs;
Provide for updates on CNPCs contact and status information on an ongoing basis;
Allow for clear and concise communication between local Emergency Management Directors (EMD), the public service company and the CNPCs;
Provide a direct communication linkage to the state EOC as it concerns CNPCs;
Assure adequate staffing levels to assist CNPCs and local EMDs to address emergency events; and
Address an understanding of the needs of each CNPC and adequately prepare to address those needs working with each CNPC.

General Plan Comments

All plans should be updated at least every two years and/or on an ongoing basis. These plans should be viewed as living documents that require ongoing attention from all levels of staff at the public service company. Updates should be shared with appropriate state agencies.
Equipment necessary for adequate levels of response should be reviewed and exercised on at least an annual basis if not more frequently.
Adequacy of staffing levels and appropriate trained staff should be reviewed on an ongoing basis.
Emergency Plans should address various levels of emergencies for various lengths of time. Staffing levels as well as equipment resources for long-term loss of service should be addressed and planned.
CNPCs with emergency generators during long-term loss of service should be prioritized for return of service.
Id., p. 8.

The Authority continues to expect that all public utilities and service providers to continue to consult with DESPP as necessary. Public utilities and service providers having a non-compliant Emergency Plan shall incorporate into their current and future Emergency Plans, as appropriate, any additional measures recommended by the Governor's Emergency Planning and Preparedness Initiative working group. The Emergency Plan shall include additional details describing the actions to be taken by the company to provide timely situational reports and data to local and state EOCs during a restoration process.
The Authority notes that the DPH recommendations are generally required by the Statute. However, the Authority will require that non-compliant public service companies and service providers review DPH’s recommendations and consult with DPH regarding their current and future Emergency Plans in order to assure that the plans appropriately address restoration priorities for CNPCs. The Authority recognizes customer confidentiality and the difficulties identifying individual residential CNPCs and the difficulties in restoring service to them as an important consideration in determining whether it is appropriate to implement the proposed recommendations.

Additionally, the intent of the Statute is to have all Emergency Plans contain the current name of the company’s contact and their phone number for emergency purposes. Due to the submission of exemption forms, information for several emergency contacts was not provided or updated. Therefore, the Authority will order all utilities and service providers that submitted an exemption form to provide the name of its emergency contact, a backup person and the telephone number(s) for each contact person or a 24/7 manned call center or answering service that can reach the emergency personnel that are on-call to the Authority, the state EOC and all the electric distribution companies and municipalities in its service territory. The Authority will require exempt companies to submit the revised Exemption Form (Appendix C) on July 1, 2016. The revised Exemption Form collects company contact information from exempt providers.
Non-Compliant Companies
Companies that failed to provide the Emergency Plans in this docket may be subject to in the imposition of civil penalties for noncompliance pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §§16-247c and 16-41. All non-compliant companies are required to file their complete Emergency Plans that incorporated all requirements discussed in this proceeding, to the Authority no later than September 19, 2014. Telecommunications companies failing to comply with the Authority’s directive may be subject to a proceeding to show cause why their Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity should not be revoked and or the companies fined pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §16247g(g). The Authority will initiate separate proceedings to address noncompliant companies.

Findings of Fact

The ILECs and some CLECs are providing VoIP services through various IPplatforms.

No water company filed an Emergency Plan in this proceeding.

Seven of 51 water companies having a WSP filed an Exemption Form.

Four water companies do not have a WSP.

Conclusion and Orders

Conclusion
All Emergency Plans filed in this docket have generally met the requirements set forth in Conn. Gen. Stat. § 16-32e(b). All non-compliant Emergency Plans should be revised, as appropriate, to incorporate the DESPP and DPH recommendations.

Orders

For the following Orders, submit an original and one copy in an envelope marked “for John Jasinski” of the required documentation to the Executive Secretary, Public Utilities Regulatory Authority, Ten Franklin Square, New Britain, CT 06051, and file an electronic version through the Authority’s website at www.ct.gov/pura. Submissions filed in compliance with Authority Orders must be identified by all three of the following: Docket Number, Title and Order Number.

The following Orders No. 1 and 2 apply to each public service company, telecommunications company, CVFA and CCFA, VoIP service provider and municipal utility furnishing electric, gas, telecommunications or water service all public utilities (Subject Companies):

In future filings of Emergency Plans, all Subject Companies shall file an index of pages indicating where the changes were made in their respective Emergency Plans compared to its last filed plan.

In future filings of Emergency Plans, all Subject Companies shall file in the Emergency Plan, the number of total customers that they served as of December 31 of the year prior to the filing.

No later than September 19, 2014, all non-compliant subject Companies shall update their Emergency Plans, as appropriate, to include the 2012 recommendations provided by the DPH and the DESPP in Sections III (A) and (B) of this Decision.

No later than September 19, 2014, the City of Groton Department of Public Utility shall file its electricity Emergency Plan that incorporates all additions described in this Decision, in accordance with Conn. Gen. Stat. §16-32e.

No later than September 19, 2014, the Norwalk 3rd Taxing District shall file its electricity Emergency Plan that incorporates all additions described in this Decision, in accordance with Conn. Gen. Stat. §16-32e.

No later than September 19, 2014, the South Norwalk Electric and Water shall file its electricity Emergency Plan that incorporates all additions described in this Decision, in accordance with Conn. Gen. Stat. §16-32e.

No later than September 19, 2014, the Town of Wallingford Department of Public Utility shall file its electricity Emergency Plan that incorporates all additions described in this Decision, in accordance with Conn. Gen. Stat. §16-32e.

No later than September 19, 2014, Norwich shall update its Emergency Plan to show the restoration times required for various levels of emergencies, in particular large outages, based on the number of customers affected and the number of personnel available for restoration efforts.(BEB)

No later than September 19, 2014, all utilities and service providers that submitted an exemption form to not file an Emergency Plan shall provide the name of its emergency contact, a backup person, and the telephone number(s) for each contact person or a 24/7 manned call center or answering service that can reach the emergency personnel that are on-call to the Authority, the EOC and all electric distribution companies and municipalities in its service territory.

No later than September 19, 2014, all non-compliant telecommunications companies and VoIP providers listed in Appendix B shall file their Emergency Plans or Exemption Forms that include the name of its emergency contact, a backup person, and the telephone number(s) for each contact person or a 24/7 manned call center or answering service that can reach the emergency personnel that are on-call, in accordance with Conn. Gen. Stat. §16-32e.

No later than September 19, 2014, all non-compliant companies shall file their Emergency Plans that incorporates all additions described in this Decision, in accordance with Conn. Gen. Stat. §16-32e.

No later than September 19, 2014, all water utilities that did not submit an Exemption Form, shall file an Exemption Form or Emergency Plan to the Authority that provides an emergency contingencies plan that includes the name of its emergency contact, a backup person, and the telephone number(s) for each contact person or a 24/7 manned call center or answering service that can reach the emergency personnel that are on-call to the Authority, the state EOC and all electric distribution companies and municipalities in its service territory. The water companies that did not submit the exemption form are listed in Attachment B.
